account: BirdCast is produced by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology with Colorado State University and now Purdue University and the University of Illinois. It forecasts nocturnal bird migration from a model trained on 23 years of weather-radar bird detections and reanalysis weather data. Houston Audubon states that its staff use the BirdCast forecast maps to track migration predictions. They issue Lights Out Action Alerts when a chance of high migration coincides with weather events. Alerts ask residents and businesses to turn off nonessential lights from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. during spring and fall migration. On 9 April 2021 the City of Houston proclaimed “Lights Out Nights” to help migrating birds. The Houston Chronicle reported on 19 April 2021 that Mayor Sylvester Turner had proclaimed Lights Out Nights for 19 April to 7 May, the span that Houston Audubon recommended. The paper also reported that the Cornell Lab and Colorado State University share BirdCast maps with Houston Audubon to predict when birds will pass through. In June 2021 a separate 21-year Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists estimated that halving lighted window area cuts collisions 11-fold in spring and 6-fold in fall. On 17 April 2022 Houston-area cities asked businesses and residents to go Lights Out for birds. On 25 August 2023 a statewide Lights Out gathering took place at Texas A&M University. No Houston collision reduction is documented.

ai_role.statement: The learned forecast model identifies the nights on which alerts are issued. The proclamation and alert program are documented by the operating partner, not the model's makers. The collision-reduction evidence comes from a separate Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists and is not specific to Houston. The counterfactual for Houston is unproven.

fields.account: BirdCast is produced by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology with Colorado State University and now Purdue University and the University of Illinois. It forecasts nocturnal bird migration from a model trained on 23 years of weather-radar bird detections and reanalysis weather data. Houston Audubon states that its staff use the BirdCast forecast maps to track migration predictions. They issue Lights Out Action Alerts when a chance of high migration coincides with weather events. Alerts ask residents and businesses to turn off nonessential lights from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. during spring and fall migration. On 9 April 2021 the City of Houston proclaimed “Lights Out Nights” to help migrating birds. The Houston Chronicle reported on 19 April 2021 that Mayor Sylvester Turner had proclaimed Lights Out Nights for 19 April to 7 May, the span that Houston Audubon recommended. The paper also reported that the Cornell Lab and Colorado State University share BirdCast maps with Houston Audubon to predict when birds will pass through. In June 2021 a separate 21-year Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists estimated that halving lighted window area cuts collisions 11-fold in spring and 6-fold in fall. On 17 April 2022 Houston-area cities asked businesses and residents to go Lights Out for birds. On 25 August 2023 a statewide Lights Out gathering took place at Texas A&M University. No Houston collision reduction is documented.

purpose: Forecast nightly bird migration intensity from weather radar and weather models so that cities, building owners and residents can reduce lighting on high-migration nights.

ratings.reason: Residents and building managers receive timed alerts, but no individual outcome is documented.
The city proclaimed Lights Out Nights and Houston Audubon issues alerts, but no source measures a change in collisions at Houston buildings.
The collision evidence is a Chicago study co-authored by BirdCast scientists; Houston's own collision change is unmeasured.
